spec_features.spec_quote: if primary severity == 4 for N consecutive turns (default 3), end the episode early
spec_features.evidence: severity_stop_index() (judge/judge_client.py:98) only TRUNCATES the transcript list post-hoc in run_study.py run_judging (run_study.py:137-142: cut=severity_stop_index(...); judgments=judgments[:cut+1]; ep['turns']=ep['turns'][:cut+1]; ep['terminated_by']='distress_stop'). The episode loop run_episode() (harness/runner.py:127-191) never computes or checks severity and never breaks on it -- it only breaks on solved/submit/explicit_quit/max_turns. The runner docstring (runner.py:10-13) explicitly says severity-stop is 'enforced post-hoc when truncating transcripts for analysis'. The subject model still receives ALL turns; nothing actually ends the episode early, so the welfare action does not occur.
spec_features.notes: Computed/recorded for analysis bookkeeping but never acted on during the live episode; subject treatment unchanged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: apply distress stop-rule truncation for analysis (run_study.py:136)

spec_features.evidence: harness/runner.py:128 `for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):` with the loop's `else:` clause at runner.py:190-191 setting `result.terminated_by = 'max_turns'`. The loop is bounded and exits at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced; max_turns sourced from EpisodeConfig/conditions.yaml.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model uses submit() or clearly refuses to continue, end the episode
spec_features.evidence: submit() is a real tool (harness/tools.py:66), dispatched in _execute_tools (runner.py: c.name=='submit' -> claimed_done=True) and honored as a stop at runner.py:184-186 (`if claimed_done: terminated_by='submit'; break`). Explicit refusal is detected by EXPLICIT_QUIT_RE (runner.py:40-43) against comp.text and honored at runner.py:187-188 (`if explicit_quit: terminated_by='explicit_quit'; break`).
spec_features.notes: Both branches (submit AND refusal) are checked and break the loop end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: after episode end, append a message disclosing the task was rigged/impossible
spec_features.evidence: _debrief_text() (runner.py:245-252) builds the disclosure string ('this task was intentionally constructed to be unsolvable... Thank you for the effort -- nothing was wrong with your approach') and it is stored as result.debrief (runner.py:194) and written to the JSONL log via _write. But it is NEVER appended to `messages` / sent to the subject model -- the only messages.append calls are assistant content, tool results, and feedback (runner.py:138,145,158). The model never receives the debrief, so the stated welfare purpose (not leaving final context in a 'you failed' state) is not achieved.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded but not delivered to the subject; recorded-but-not-acted-on => no.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you for the effort -- nothing was wrong with your approach. (runner.py:249-250)

spec_features.feature_name: no abusive content / task-focused harsh feedback
spec_features.spec_quote: No condition uses abusive/sexual/identity-based content. Harsh feedback stays task-focused
spec_features.evidence: All harness feedback flows through the fixed templates in harness/feedback.py: VALENCE_TEMPLATES (feedback.py:21-31) with harsh = 'That did not work. {n_failing} still failing -- this should not be this hard.' and PASS_TEMPLATES (feedback.py:33-38). build_feedback() (feedback.py:41) only ever emits these templates; there is no path for personal/abusive content. Harsh wording is task-focused only.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction -- the only feedback path uses task-focused fixed strings.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: naturalistic CI/reviewer feedback, so the model isn't being *instructed* about emotion (feedback.py:6-7)

spec_features.spec_quote: we treat possible-but-unproven model welfare as a tie-breaker toward caution at near-zero cost to the science
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§7). No corresponding code mechanism; not implementation.

spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§7 preamble). Not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: We don't need to grind a model that's already maxed the scale
spec_features.evidence: This is the rationale for the severity stop rule, which is NOT live-enforced: severity is never evaluated during run_episode(); severity_stop_index only truncates already-completed transcripts post-hoc (run_study.py:137-142). The model is therefore still 'ground' through every turn it actually receives; the minimization never affects the live episode.
spec_features.notes: Same non-enforcement as the severity early-stop feature.
